# C# — type semantics before frameworks

Each code block is a **separate C# example**. The main goal is to understand the type system and lifetime of data, not build a large application.

## 1. Value types versus reference types

~~~csharp
int x = 3;
int y = x;
y = 9;
Console.WriteLine(x); // 3
~~~

Two integer variables contain independent values. A class instance is a reference type: two variables can point to the same object. Structs are value types (with caveats for fields that themselves refer to objects).

## 2. Nullable references express a possibility

~~~csharp
string? name = null;
Console.WriteLine(name?.Length ?? 0); // 0
~~~

The question mark declares that the variable may contain null (in a nullable-enabled context). The null-conditional and null-coalescing operators handle that possibility without dereferencing null.

## 3. Records describe data with value-based equality

~~~csharp
Console.WriteLine(new User(7) == new User(7)); // True
record User(int Id);
~~~

A record class provides generated value equality for its components, unlike ordinary reference equality on a simple class. Reference-type components still require careful consideration of their own equality and mutability.

## 4. Pattern matching narrows cases

~~~csharp
static string Describe(object x) => x switch {
    int n when n > 0 => "positive",
    int => "other integer",
    _ => "other type"
};
Console.WriteLine(Describe(3)); // positive
~~~

Cases are matched top to bottom. The variable n becomes available only in the matching case.

## 5. Async methods return a Task

~~~csharp
static async Task<int> AnswerAsync() {
    await Task.Delay(1);
    return 42;
}
Console.WriteLine(await AnswerAsync()); // 42
~~~

Await suspends the method while the asynchronous operation completes; it is not a request to create a new OS thread for every call.

## 6. LINQ queries are often deferred

~~~csharp
int[] a = { 1, 2, 3 };
var odds = a.Where(x => x % 2 == 1);
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", odds)); // 1,3
~~~

Where creates an enumerable sequence. Evaluating it later can see a changed source collection; materialise with ToList when a snapshot is required.

**Official reference:** [C# Language Reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/), [Asynchronous programming](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/asynchronous-programming/).
